UC San Diego Health is proud to be a four-time Magnet-designated organization and has now earned Magnet with Distinction from the American Nurses Credentialing Center (ANCC). Magnet is the gold standard for nursing excellence, achieved by only about 10% of hospitals worldwide. Magnet with Distinction is awarded to the highest-performing Magnet organizations, with only a select few earning this prestigious honor. This recognition reflects our commitment to transformational leadership, professional nursing excellence, innovation, exceptional patient outcomes, and an empowering practice environment where nurses thrive.

UC San Diego Health is seeking an experienced and collaborative Infusion Admin Nurse to support daily operations within our Infusion Services program. This unique leadership role combines clinical expertise with operational oversight, serving as both a frontline clinical resource and an administrative leader to ensure safe, efficient, and patient-centered care.

Under the direction of Infusion Services leadership, the Infusion Admin Nurse supports the daily clinical and operational functions of the Infusion Services program. Serving as a clinical expert and frontline leader, this role provides direct clinical support while coordinating dailyoperations to ensure safe, efficient, and patient-centered care delivery.

The Infusion Admin Nurse partners closely with nursing leadership, physicians, advanced practice providers, pharmacy, scheduling teams, and frontline staff to optimize patient throughput, staffing, and workflow efficiency. This position plays a key leadership role in managing patient flow, coordinating staffing resources and break coverage, overseeing infusion overbook requests, addressing operational challenges, and supporting charge nurse responsibilities as needed.

As a primary resource for frontline staff, the Infusion Admin Nurse provides real-time clinical guidance, supports weekend operations, facilitates communication across interdisciplinary teams, and assists in resolving patient, provider, and staff concerns. The role also contributes to onboarding, staff development, quality improvement initiatives, regulatory compliance, and operational excellence through continuous evaluation and enhancement of workflows, patient access, and service delivery.
This role is ideal for an experienced oncology or infusion nurse who enjoys operational leadership, problem-solving, and mentoring others while remaining engaged in clinical care
Strong critical thinking and clinical decision-making abilities.
Demonstrated ability to coordinate patient flow, prioritize competing demands, and make operational decisions in a fast-paced infusion environment.
Excellent communication, interpersonal, and organizational skills.
Proven ability to collaborate effectively with interdisciplinary teams.
